question_text:
The students at Hoylebury Middle School are to be surveyed on their attitudes on wearing school uniform. The numbers of students in each year level are shown.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
& \text{Boys} & \text{Girls} \\
\hline
\text{Year 8} & 135 & 140 \\
\hline
\text{Year 9} & 130 & 145 \\
\hline
\text{Year 10} & 125 & 130 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

subparts.stem: What are the advantages of surveying 50 students?
subparts.final_answer: $A survey of 50 students is manageable in time and sufficiently representative of the student body.$

mark_breakdown.desc: State that 50 students is feasible within time constraints and large enough to be representative

subparts.solution: A survey of 50 students can be completed in a reasonable time frame. It is also large enough that the results can be representative of the whole student body.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: An effective sample balances practical constraints (time, cost) with statistical validity (representativeness).
step_by_step: Consider the feasibility in terms of time and resources.
Consider whether the sample is large enough to reflect the target population.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Failing to mention both the practical benefit and representativeness.

subparts.stem: What are the disadvantages of surveying all students?
subparts.final_answer: $Surveying all students is time-consuming and risks non-response error due to absences.$

mark_breakdown.desc: Explain that surveying all students is impractical/time-consuming and risks non-response error

subparts.solution: Surveying all students is time-consuming and often impractical. A non-response error may be produced if students are absent.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: A full census is often resource-intensive and prone to non-response bias when members of the population are unavailable.
step_by_step: Identify the difficulty and time required to survey an entire population.
Note the potential for missing data (non-response error) from absent students.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Assuming a census always gives perfect data without considering absent individuals.

subparts.stem: A stratified sample system is used to select 50 students. How many Year 8 boys will be selected?

mark_breakdown.desc: Calculate total population and set up proportional stratified formula

subparts.solution: Total number of students $= 135 + 140 + 130 + 145 + 125 + 130 = 805$. For the survey, $\frac{135}{805} \times 50 \approx 8$ Year 8 boys will be selected.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Stratified sampling allocates sample size proportionally: $n_i = \frac{N_i}{N} \times n$.
step_by_step: Calculate stratum proportion for Year 8 boys: $\frac{135}{805}$.
Round to the nearest whole person: $8$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Rounding to the wrong whole number or calculating out of total boys instead of total students.

subparts.stem: How many girls will be selected in total?

mark_breakdown.desc: Find total number of girls across all year levels

subparts.solution: For the survey, $\frac{140 + 145 + 130}{805} \times 50 = \frac{415}{805} \times 50 \approx 26$ girls will be selected.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Stratified sampling requires finding the total count of the specified subgroup over the entire population.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Selecting only one year level of girls instead of all girls.

subparts.stem: Explain why a stratified sample is better than a random sample in this case.
subparts.final_answer: $A stratified sample guarantees fair representation of each year level and gender, unlike a random sample.$

mark_breakdown.desc: Explain that stratified sampling guarantees proportional representation of each stratum

subparts.solution: A stratified sample is better than a random sample in this case as a stratified sample will fairly represent each year level and gender. A random sample cannot guarantee such a fair representation.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Stratified sampling ensures subgroups with known characteristics are proportionally represented, preventing accidental under- or over-representation that may occur in simple random sampling.
step_by_step: Compare how simple random sampling can introduce imbalance purely by chance.
State that stratified sampling preserves subgroup proportions (gender and year levels).
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Stating that random sampling is always inferior without citing subgroup representation.
